Mientras que en BAS los tonos tienen una función gramatical central, ésta es marginal en TAT. El sistema BAS es un sistema tonal restringido que puede ser analizado, tanto como un sistema tonal como un sistema de acento tonal (pitch accent). He intentado una interpretación como acento tonal [GOM 97a, GOM.KEN 00] y como tonos [GOM 99, 00, 01, 03], y finalmente prefiero el análisis tonal porque da cuenta satisfactoriamente de procesos como (27) ... sweep_summary: Barasana-Eduria (bara1380, catalog kind 'tonal', deciding source Gómez-Imbert 2004-05 Amerindia). All five sweep items are Gómez-Imbert works already known to be about the tone/pitch-accent system (three are duplicate Glottolog records of the 2001 ILCAA chapter). None could be opened: (1) Gómez-Imbert & Kenstowicz 2000 IJAL remains paywalled — the 'GREEN' OA pointer in OpenAlex/Unpaywall/Semantic Scholar is an Icesi DSpace metadata record whose only bitstream is a 255-byte redirect to the DOI (saved as receipt); its abstract (Semantic Scholar, French) calls Barasana a tone language whose F0 contour is set by autosegmental tone distribution over the metrical grid, with pitch accent a property of the morpheme — consistent with the catalog's tonal/pitch-accent coding. (2) The 2001 ILCAA chapter (Kaji ed., ISBN 4872977947, CiNii BA54654809) is print-only; Gómez-Imbert 2004-05 herself calls it 'la mejor presentación tonal' — highest acquisition priority. (3) Cahiers de Grammaire 22 (1997) is not online (ERSS server holds only vols 24-30) and, from how the author cites it, concerns moraic/prosodic structure and segmental processes rather than accent placement — low priority. Additionally read the open Cahiers de Grammaire 24 (1999) paper already on file: it states Barasana 'peut être analysé comme un accent tonal à deux mélodies, H et HB' (p. 75) and is 'un accent tonal d'un point de vue typologique' (p. 81), with four root melodies H/HL/LH/LHL (p. 82) — confirms the catalog coding; it does not supersede the 2004-05 deciding source. OpenAlex returned 429 throughout; archive.org was offline.

new_statements.locator: p. 75 (sec. 1) and p. 81 (sec. 2.1); lexical melodies p. 82 sec. 2.2 ex. (7)
new_statements.reading: First-hand statement by the principal describer: Barasana has two surface tones H/L and is typologically a pitch-accent (or restricted tone) system with two lexical melodies (H, HL), roots bimoraic with four surface melodies H/HL/LH/LHL, initial L handled by left-edge extrametricality, tonal prefixes on verbs. No syllable-counting or weight-based stress rule; the Jones & Jones 'phonemic stress' is the same pitch phenomenon. This confirms the catalog coding (tonal / TONAL-OR-PITCH-ACCENT).

sources.quote: L'A. examine le systeme tonique et accentuel du barasama, langue a tons presentant deux caracteristiques : 1. le contour F0 est determine par des principes autosegmentaux distribuant les tons via la grille metrique, 2. l'accent de hauteur est une propriete du morpheme. Puis l'A. se concentre sur trois constructions dans lesquelles l'accent de hauteur de la tete propositionnelle est supplante par un accent determine par l'element precedent. [...] Il termine par une comparaison entre le barasana et le japonais
